A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same HyCoCLIP research. Their text, equations, tables, figures and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching retained material across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification, retrieval, detection, hierarchical classification and scene-understanding results, alongside ablations and representation analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds curvature experiments, HierarCaps evaluation and comparative interpolation results.

M1.justification: The encoders, grounding pipeline and compositional contrastive and entailment objectives remain unchanged. Both versions use learnable curvature initialized at 1.0. The added fixed-curvature experiments are ablations; the newly documented curvature bounds do not establish a change to the underlying method.

E1.justification: v2 adds HierarCaps for hierarchical image-text matching against four hierarchically relevant captions per image, extending evaluation beyond the existing ImageNet/WordNet hierarchy task. Training corpora and previous downstream coverage remain. RedCaps was already used in v1.

E2.justification: v2 adds CLIP and MERU as explicit comparators for the existing interpolation examples, which previously displayed only HyCoCLIP outputs. Existing quantitative comparator sets, including RegionCLIP, remain unchanged. HierarCaps uses the established CLIP/MERU comparator set.

E3.justification: Added experiments introduce fixed-curvature controls trained on grounded CC3M for 40k steps and a HierarCaps protocol using 50 root-to-nearest-text interpolation points, four reference captions, precision, recall and ordering metric τd. The new CLIP interpolation comparison uses the training-embedding centroid as its root. Existing experimental protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Supplementary analysis expands substantially through a fixed-versus-learnable curvature ablation (Table 7), matched CLIP/MERU comparisons across the retained interpolation cases, and HierarCaps qualitative matching examples (Figure 11). These add direct controls for curvature choice and comparative evidence about hierarchical organization. Existing loss, batch-size and aperture analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report experimental point estimates without repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals or significance tests. The additional results do not introduce a different uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: v2 adds a HyCoCLIP RedCaps row, fixed-curvature outcomes, HierarCaps results and baseline interpolation outputs; retained numerical results are unchanged. Table 10 reports precision/recall/τd of 0.12/0.46/0.88 for HyCoCLIP, 0.13/0.29/0.83 for CLIP and 0.12/0.39/0.84 for MERU. Thus, the new matching results favor HyCoCLIP in recall and ordering, but not precision.

T1.justification: The Lorentz geometry, learning objectives, hierarchical classification formulas and interpolation mathematics in Equations 1–16 are retained. No substantive mathematical revision, theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: compositional entailment learning, improved downstream performance and stronger hierarchical representations. The new evaluations support these existing claims without redefining their scope.

C2.justification: The explanations concerning grounding quality, generic box negatives, representation hierarchy and retrieval tradeoffs remain. The conclusion retains the same bounding-box preprocessing and retrieval limitations. New appendix commentary reports additional findings and reiterates the existing hierarchical interpretation.

D1.justification: v2 replaces the promised code release with a concrete repository link and newly specifies curvature clamping within [0.1, 10.0]. This is additional access and implementation documentation; the PDFs do not establish that clamping was newly introduced. Existing architecture, optimizer and hardware details remain.

R1.justification: v2 adds Alper and Averbuch-Elor for HierarCaps, Ibrahimi et al. on spatial awareness, and additional hyperbolic-learning references, including Mandica et al. The central positioning relative to CLIP, MERU and compositional hierarchies remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Edits include condensing the contribution bullets into a numbered paragraph, moving hierarchical classification before detection, expanding selected appendix explanations, and updating affiliations, acknowledgements and conference headers. Most existing scientific prose and the overall narrative structure are retained.

P2.justification: The existing interpolation examples are rebuilt into multicolumn HyCoCLIP/MERU/CLIP comparisons in Figures 12–16. v2 also adds GRIT sample illustrations, HierarCaps qualitative displays and two experimental tables. Table highlighting and captions are refined, while retained appendix figures and tables are relocated and renumbered.

improvement.justification: The HierarCaps evaluation and matched interpolation comparisons provide more direct evidence for the existing hierarchy claim, while the curvature ablation and code link improve experimental support and documentation. These incrementally strengthen an already evaluated method. Appendix H's broad outperformance wording overlooks the absence of a precision advantage in Table 10, but this limited overstatement does not outweigh the added evidence.
